blocks.text: Like anyone with a sound mind, I do not believe in ghosts or any form of the dead returning.
And whilst I have, on one occasion in my life, taken part in a table-turning séance, the reason was simply the lively, good company gathered round.

But what of those who have died and return in our dreams – nightmares, for the most part – haunting and inhabiting them, reminding us of the shortcomings and lapses in attention we showed towards them when they were living beings around us, and often very close to us?

What can be said of what they leave behind, and which, to get rid of, would be to inflict a second death upon them; of what we leave, and will leave, behind us, with both feet in the grave, and to which we were so attached—things we had sometimes struggled so hard to acquire, at the cost of such efforts and sacrifices?
Or what do our past loves—whether succubi or incubi—leave behind them?
“The final act is bloody, however fine the play may be in all the rest; at last, earth is thrown upon the head, and that is the end of it for ever.” Pascal, Pensées 154 Folio/le Guern.
